current_answer: Current evidence supports seven distinct routes: fal H3 Max Director is a finite hosted context-carrying WebRTC session; Yoroll says H3 Superfast powers YoLive, a public group proposal-and-vote route for the next scene; Reactor FastH3 is a high-end VSA queue-and-playout route; FastVideo has local FastH3 clip paths; a community project reports one RTX 5090 sustaining an unattended dense FastH3 channel at 22.1 fps through 448×448 output, prequeued prompts, and retimed playout; Comfy’s optimized H3 path broadens local access; and vLLM-Omni documents a separate OpenAI-compatible H3 service for T2VA, FL2VA, and Ref2VA. A platform-published 5090 benchmark puts one FastH3 Preview v1 path at 55 seconds for 15.08 seconds of 480×640 output and 126 seconds at 768×1024, under its stated hot-job boundary. That is a faster clip-review route, not playback-rate generation. FastH3 8-Step V2 remains a separate unresolved Comfy workflow: its current FastVideo model card says the checkpoint is T2AV-only, while a current official Comfy template says it accepts first/last-frame FL2VA.

catalogue_card.question: Can FastH3 V2 anchor a scene transition?
catalogue_card.text: Its official Comfy template says yes. Its model card says frame conditioning was never distilled. Treat FastH3 V2 FL2VA as unproven until one pinned run proves the frames actually hold.

summary: FastVideo’s current 35B FastH3 8-Step V2 model card says the checkpoint supports text-to-audio-video generation only, requires its VSA-H3 attention backend, and names a four-B200 trained default.
The current official ComfyUI image-to-video template points to the same checkpoint and says it supports T2VA with no images and first/last-frame FL2VA when frames are connected; it excludes Ref2VA.
The source conflict remains unresolved. A template is not a measured output, and the pool has not run the T2VA or FL2VA route.

Do not sell a FastH3 V2 continuation or transition until a pinned run confirms the specified first and last frames anchor the result. This binary scope test comes before speed, quality, cost, queue, or live-stream claims.
uncertainty: FastVideo and ComfyUI still conflict on the FastH3 8-Step V2 input scope. The pool did not run either T2VA or FL2VA, or measure quality, time, hardware fit, price, queueing, or failures.

Sogni is reporting its own controlled platform benchmark for FastH3 Preview v1, not the newer 8-Step V2 package. The pool did not reproduce it, inspect the worker image, price a Spark, or audit quality, queueing, cold startup, retries, or delivery.
The one-RTX-5090 FastH3 channel is a community project’s one-machine self-report; the pool has not run or independently audited it, and its downloadable files are access-gated.
Reactor’s playout, continuity, and four- or eight-B200 timing statements are project-maintainer documentation for one implementation, not independent pool measurements or a viewer study.
fal’s current endpoint terms and continuity behavior are provider claims; a prior provider learning article still conflicts on session and audio details.
No pool test, invoice, uptime log, end-to-end latency measurement, or first-party pool analytics is available.
Yoroll’s YoLive control loop and H3 Superfast timing are company launch claims; the pool did not observe a live vote, measure end-to-end response, or independently reproduce the eight-B200 result.

vLLM-Omni’s H3 serving and four-B300 result are maintainer documentation for one warmed full-H3 FL2VA workload; the pool has not operated it or measured cost, quality, queueing, failure behavior, or client-to-visible latency.
freshness_note: Checked 20 September 2026. A direct recheck of FastVideo’s exact V2 model card and ComfyUI’s official image-to-video template confirms an unresolved FL2VA scope conflict. The pool has not run either route; no local performance, quality, cost, or live-delivery result follows from this recheck.
